experiment: Voxel session J (combined paper W3): Nsight Compute counters for the FP64 element-product kernels on an RTX 4090 inside a vast.ai KVM virtual machine
status_at_declaration: Declared before any session J rental. Containers refused counters on every host in session F; this probes a full VM, where root owns the driver.
questions: Q1: are counters readable in a VM (no ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM)?

H15: on the RTX 4090, do dense8, modal8 and modal8_muladd each run at >= 70 % of FP64 pipe peak (sm__pipe_fp64_cycles_active, pct of peak sustained active), and do issued FP64 thread instructions (DADD+DMUL+DFMA) scale 78:52:34 within 5 % (ratios dense8/modal8_muladd and modal8/modal8_muladd)?
Descriptive: the same counters for fused_ai_fp64 and node_fp64, DRAM throughput and L2 reduction (atomic) sectors.

ncu.metric_filter: metrics absent from `ncu --query-metrics` are dropped and recorded; H15 needs the FP64 pipe and op-count metrics

decision.counters_available: every kernel profiled with exit 0 and no ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM
decision.H15: pipe utilization >= 70 % for dense8, modal8 and modal8_muladd, and |measured/static - 1| <= 0.05 for dense8/modal8_muladd (static 78/34) and modal8/modal8_muladd (static 52/34), using issued FP64 thread instructions
decision.if_unavailable: W3 is closed as unavailable on the providers tried; the paper states that the FP64-issue mechanism is inferred from static counts and timing

not_claimed: Counter values describe one launch per kernel on one host and grid; they explain mechanism, not speed.
